editorial_thesis: The strongest fresh signal is operational control at the seams: manage model replacement, keep agent interactions private and bounded, and make workflow execution and AI spend attributable.

topic_groups.title: Model Portfolio Change Control
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A coverage gap between model-choice governance and day-to-day operations: two fresh GitHub changes make model retirement and role-scoped access concrete administrative work rather than a quarterly policy exercise.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash deprecated
sources.why_selected: A model picker is not a stable interface. Prompts, latency assumptions, and output review expectations need an owned replacement path.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: add model IDs and fallback acceptance tests to every agent runbook. Client work: prepare a one-page migration note before a preferred model disappears.

sources.title: Enterprise teams model policy targeting
sources.why_selected: It enables role-based frontier-model pilots without granting every employee the same catalog.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: propose a “pilot / production / prohibited” model matrix. Client work: scope privileged models to trained delivery teams.

sources.title: Managing availability of Copilot models
sources.why_selected: The documentation provides the control-plane checklist needed to turn the preview into an auditable rollout.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: capture the pre-switch policy export. Client work: assign model ownership to enterprise administrators.

topic_groups.title: Private Agent Channel Controls
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A neglected collaboration lane with practical fresh signal: targeted in-channel responses have reached Teams, while device-scoped Copilot remote-control policies provide a complementary boundary for where an operator can take over.

sources.title: Chat SDK reactions and ephemeral messages on Teams
sources.why_selected: Permission requests and private diagnostics no longer need to spill into a shared project channel; reactions can make long-running work legible.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: acknowledge intake with a reaction, send approval prompts privately, and publish only the final artifact to the shared thread. Client work: implement a consistent Teams agent interaction contract.

sources.title: Ephemeral Messages — Chat SDK
sources.why_selected: The same API has materially different records behavior across Teams, Slack, Google Chat, and Discord.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: define which approvals must become durable tickets. Client work: choose DM fallback deliberately, not as an accidental audit trail.

sources.title: Limit remote control to managed devices
sources.why_selected: Remote control changes the risk profile of an agent session; device posture is a useful enforcement layer beyond an account policy.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: keep remote control disabled on shared runners. Client work: deploy requireSSO through MDM for approved operator workstations.

topic_groups.title: Attributed Workflow Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A practical operations lane separated from the recently covered agent-economics theme: fresh Vercel releases make both individual workflow investigations and tag-level AI cost attribution more usable in the same operating loop.

sources.title: Expanded search for workflow runs in Vercel Observability
sources.why_selected: An incident can now be narrowed to a reproducible slice instead of a vague time window.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: place a stable run attribute on every client workflow. Client work: add a saved incident query to each runbook.

sources.title: Custom reporting on AI Gateway
sources.why_selected: It can make agent margins and client allocations inspectable without maintaining a separate provider-console spreadsheet.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: tag every request with client, workflow, environment, and service tier. Client work: export a weekly feature-cost view.

sources.title: Vercel Observability documentation
sources.why_selected: It supplies the broader causal trail around a workflow run: route, function, external dependency, then model request.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: link workflow run IDs from delivery artifacts. Client work: use project-level views for service debugging and team-level views for portfolio patterns.
